**Explanation:**
The manipulation of time in this passage (which is the famous opening of Theodor Fontane's classic novel *Effi Briest*) is masterfully balanced to fit the atmosphere of the scene. The author uses a technique akin to "stretching" or pausing story time—spending an entire paragraph describing a single, static midday moment ("mittagsstille"). By slowing the narrative pace to a virtual standstill to detail the architecture, the garden, the shadows, and the objects on the table, the real-world reading time is stretched out. This slow, deliberate pacing perfectly mirrors the tranquil, unhurried, and somewhat stagnant nature of aristocratic country life on a hot afternoon, while simultaneouslycompressing centuries of family history ("seit Kurfürst Georg Wilhelm") into a single opening clause to establish tradition and permanence.
